SCHOOL ROOM · THE ART ROOM · 27 CARDS · AGES 2–5

The Art Room — every card carries a thing to make.

Twenty-seven supplies, twenty-seven activities: draw a picture with shapes, shape a tiny animal, mix two colours together, cut out simple shapes. Every card prints one make-it activity under its name, every supply has its own short page, its own lesson and a printable twin — and the room runs on the youngest rule in the school: make something, make a mess, make it again.

Open the supply shelf ↓The printable set ↗
HOW THIS ROOM WORKS

Read the card. Make the thing. Then go deeper.

Every card in this deck does two jobs: it names one art supply and it prints one activity — a make-it line the card means literally. The short pages on this shelf show each card, quote its activity word for word, and add one way to set the supply up tonight. When one supply becomes a favorite, its lesson page carries the full teaching — what the tool is, what the activity secretly trains, the parent script, the questions to ask — and the library page holds the printable twin with a download button.

The shelf runs in file order like a real room: the drawing tools first, then the paint and print crew, then the cut-and-stick builders, and the studio furniture at the end. For color work beyond this room, the Colors extra class hunts every shade the house hides, and the Coloring Pages keep print-and-color days stocked when the paints are still drying from yesterday.

ALL TWENTY-SEVEN SUPPLIES

Meet the shelf — cover to watercolors.

Every card in the owner’s file order: chalk, clay, colored pencils and cotton balls open the shelf; crayons, paint, scissors and glue carry the middle; and the studio furniture closes it. Tap any card to open its short page.

GAMES THE ART ROOM PLAYS

When the glue is drying, play.

Art time and game time trade places all afternoon, and the school’s games shelf holds the rules for the games this room plays best: the Colour Hunt turns the whole house into a color deck, the Shape Hunt finds the shapes chalk pictures are built from, Shadow Shapes poses drawings against the wall, and Follow the Leader is a copy-me drawing game with no pencil at all. Full rules on every page — the paint pots can wait.

AROUND THE SCHOOL

Where to wander next.

Explore the School — every room, one door each ↗Print a Coloring Page for quiet table time ↗Hunt colors in the Colors extra class · Ages 2–5 ↗

The Art Room sits on the school’s room shelf beside the Library, the Garden, the Playground and the Music Room. The Colors class is its closest cousin — fifteen spotter sheets for the shades this room paints with — and the Coloring Pages are its quiet corner: bold outlines, one download each, no setup at all.

Making is the curriculum. Every activity on these cards hides real work — grips, pressure, planning, patience — inside something the child thinks is just today’s craft. Do the thing first; the skills follow the glue.

HOLIDAY CRAFTS

Make it for the celebration.

Every holiday needs glue: paper ghosts and painted pumpkins for Halloween, handprint turkeys for Thanksgiving, hearts for Valentine’s Day, crescent moons for Eid. The school’s School Hall keeps the holiday calendar — the next celebration first — and every holiday page there carries printable cards that pair with the make-it activities in this room: craft here, celebrate there.

FLASHCARDS

Prefer printed cards?

The cards from this class also live in the flashcards library — every card has its own page with the picture, the words to say together and a download button, ready for away-from-screen time.
